### Personal projects

#### Sydney (Personal AI assistant · in daily use since 2026)
An assistant that lives in a Telegram chat. You write to her the way you'd tell a person — “pay the electricity bill friday” — and she files it with the date already set. Real users rely on her every day.
- Talk, don't fill forms: Tasks from plain sentences. Dates are read out of the sentence and shown back before saving — a wrong date is invisible until the reminder fires on the wrong day.
- Two briefings a day: Morning: what's coming. Evening: what's still open. Sent to each user at their own local time.
- Calendar & email: Add events, see the day, triage the inbox. Surfaces only the emails from real people that actually need a reply.
- Money owed: Who owes you, and what you owe. Tracked per user, in a shared spreadsheet.
- Voice notes: Speak instead of typing. Transcribed automatically, then handled like any message.
- Private by design: Invite-only; each user sees only their own data. Access is decided in one place, and a rejected sign-in never reveals who has an account.
How I handled the hardest problem:
- Problem: Users told me the assistant sometimes confirmed a task as done when it wasn't. For an assistant, trust is the product: one false “done” and people stop relying on it.
- Diagnosis: The obvious fix — stricter instructions to the AI — was tried three times and failed three times. Instructions can ask; they can't enforce.
- Fix: I moved the guarantee out of the AI and into the system: every reply is checked against what actually happened. An unverified claim is retried once, then replaced with an honest “I couldn't do that.”
- Result: Users get the action or the truth — never a false confirmation. Same principle I use in operations: controls, not reminders.
Stack: Node.js, OpenAI GPT-5 mini, MCP, Next.js, TypeScript, Postgres, Vercel
Links: Live web app: https://task-dashboard-six-snowy.vercel.app · Assistant code: https://github.com/slabarcaf/melissa-bot · Web app code: https://github.com/slabarcaf/task-dashboard

#### Form auto-register bot (Automation · weekly job)
A weekly sign-up arrives by email as a brand-new Google Form — new link, new fields, every time. This bot finds it, understands it, and submits it on my behalf.
- Finds the form: Reads the weekly email. Nothing about the form is hard-coded — it's rediscovered every run.
- Never double-submits: Remembers what it already did. Safe to re-run at any time.
- Fails loudly: If anything breaks, I get a message. With a one-tap link to finish it by hand.
What changed along the way:
- Plan: Submit the form directly, with nothing to install.
- Finding: Submissions were rejected: the form requires a signed-in Google account, even though anyone can view it.
- Pivot: Scrapped the plan and moved to a signed-in browser that fills and submits the form automatically.
Stack: Node.js, Playwright, Gmail API, Telegram
Links: Code is private — ask me for a walkthrough
